PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.

items.rationale: Policy 7.1.10 and 3.1.6: The frame is only indemnified if it is an affected item (i.e., physically damaged in the theft). The description and photo confirm the bike took a knock and the frame needed replacement. However, the bicycle is scheduled at an agreed value of EUR 3,500, which is the ceiling for all indemnity (including repair, replacement, and recovery costs) for this item. The frame is part of the scheduled item, so indemnity is possible, but the total for all lines relating to the bike (including recovery) cannot exceed EUR 3,500. Reference Case 23 shows that if the bike is recovered and nobody is paid for the frame, t = 0. Here, the frame is physically damaged and replaced, so indemnity is likely.

Policy 7.1.10 and 3.1.6: The brakes are only indemnified if they are an affected item (i.e., physically damaged in the theft). The description states the brakes needed replacement due to the theft. Reference Case 23 shows that if the bike is recovered and nobody is paid for the brakes, t = 0. Here, the brakes are physically damaged and replaced, so indemnity is likely, but the total for all lines relating to the bike (including recovery) cannot exceed EUR 3,500.
Policy 7.1.8(d) and price priors: Shipping is not indemnified in any reference case and is excluded as an ancillary charge not specifically covered.

Policy 7.1.7(g) and price priors: Vehicle costs are indemnified if they relate to covered repair/recovery work. Reference cases show t per pc about 77 when indemnified. Here, the vehicle cost is for the bicycle service, which is part of the repair of an affected item.

Policy 7.1.7(c) and price priors: Assembly costs are indemnified if they relate to covered repair/recovery work. Reference cases show t per pc about 109 when indemnified. Here, the assembly cost is for the bicycle service, which is part of the repair of an affected item.
Policy 7.1.8(d) and price priors: Miscellaneous items are not indemnified in any reference case and are excluded as ancillary charges not specifically covered.

Policy 7.1.7(d) and price priors: Apprentice hours are indemnified if they relate to covered repair/recovery work. Reference cases show t per hr about 36 when indemnified. Here, the apprentice hour is for the bicycle service, which is part of the repair of an affected item.
Policy 7.1.7(d) and price priors: Skilled worker hours are not indemnified in any reference case and are excluded as ancillary charges not specifically covered.

Policy 5.2.2 and price priors: Vehicle costs are indemnified if they relate to the recovery of an item that was taken. Here, the locksmith's attendance was necessary to recover the stolen bicycle, so this is a covered recovery cost. Reference cases show t per pc about 77 when indemnified.

Policy 5.2.2(b) and price priors: Assembly costs (here, the lock cutting) are indemnified as part of the necessary recovery work to release the bicycle. Reference cases show t per pc about 109 when indemnified.
Policy 7.1.8(d) and price priors: Miscellaneous items are not indemnified in any reference case and are excluded as ancillary charges not specifically covered.
Policy 5.2.2(b) and price priors: Apprentice hours are indemnified if they relate to the necessary recovery work. Reference cases show t per hr about 36 when indemnified.
Policy 5.2.2(b) and price priors: Skilled worker hours are not indemnified in any reference case and are excluded as ancillary charges not specifically covered.
